lead.headline: Polymarket's $1B Trump-linked raise signals prediction markets as new political infrastructure
lead.tldr: This week, capital formation and regulatory access in crypto converged around political proximity: Polymarket's billion-dollar Trump Jr.-linked round, Hyperliquid's White House invitation, and institutional stablecoin launches all suggest the market is repricing 'regulatory risk' as 'regulatory allocation'—where the prize goes to those with Beltway access, not just technical merit.

intro: Dear Founders, Investors, and Friends, this week the signals read less like technology news and more like a political economy map—capital is flowing to protocols that can secure regulatory air cover, while traditional finance builds parallel rails that may obsolete the public blockchain experiments they now appear to embrace.

top_signals.title: Trump Jr.-linked 1789 Capital leads Polymarket’s $1B raise: Report26m
top_signals.summary: Polymarket has reportedly raised $1 billion in a funding round led by 1789 Capital, a firm linked to Donald Trump Jr. This massive capital injection highlights the growing institutional interest in prediction markets and decentralized betting platforms.
top_signals.why_it_matters: A $1 billion raise for a prediction market at this valuation, led by a Trump-linked vehicle, is not a bet on consumer demand for election betting—it is a wager that political information markets will be licensed as infrastructure rather than shut down as gambling, and that proximity to the administration secures that license.

top_signals.title: President Trump says he wants Hyperliquid to enter the US — here’s how it could happen
top_signals.summary: President Trump has expressed a desire to bring the decentralized exchange Hyperliquid into the United States. This signal suggests a potential shift in regulatory approach toward prominent DeFi protocols.
top_signals.why_it_matters: When a President names a specific DeFi protocol for US market entry, the signal is not regulatory clarity but regulatory favoritism—founders should model their go-to-market on lobbying capacity as much as code quality, and investors should price political optionality into DeFi valuations.

top_signals.title: 🫂 Nvidia Takes Hugging Face Into Its Embrace With $12.9b Acquisition Deal
top_signals.summary: Nvidia has entered into a $12.9 billion acquisition deal to acquire Hugging Face. The move is described as both a defensive and offensive strategic maneuver to strengthen its position in the AI ecosystem.
top_signals.why_it_matters: Nvidia's $12.9 billion Hugging Face acquisition tightens the AI compute-stack monopoly and raises the defensive cost of entry for any crypto-AI convergence play; the strategic takeaway is that middleware layers without distribution or silicon access are being squeezed from both ends.

top_signals.title: South Korea to start tokenizing 'all types' of securities in three stages from 2027
top_signals.summary: South Korea has announced a three-stage strategic plan starting in 2027 to tokenize all types of securities. The long-term goal is to enable the on-chain settlement of these tokenized assets using stablecoins.
top_signals.why_it_matters: South Korea's three-stage tokenization roadmap with stablecoin settlement by 2027 sets a regulatory benchmark that will cascade through Asian capital markets; the test is whether on-chain settlement reduces friction enough to justify the operational overhaul, or whether it becomes a parallel system that banks run for compliance theater.

top_signals.title: BofA, Citi, Goldman Sachs among 21 institutions planning stablecoin launch
top_signals.summary: Twenty-one major financial institutions, including BofA, Citi, and Goldman Sachs, are collaborating on a new digital money venture. The initiative focuses on enhancing cross-border payments and settlement with a planned launch in 2027.
top_signals.why_it_matters: Twenty-one major banks coordinating on a 2027 stablecoin launch is not adoption of public crypto rails but an attempt to preempt them with permissioned alternatives; the repricing risk is that DeFi stablecoin issuers have overestimated their regulatory runway and underestimated the speed of bank consortium response.

top_signals.title: London Stock Exchange partners with Kraken parent for tokenized UK stocks: FT
top_signals.summary: The London Stock Exchange has partnered with Kraken's parent company to enable the trading of tokenized UK stocks. The initiative aims to provide 24/5 market access starting in 2027.
top_signals.why_it_matters: The LSE-Kraken partnership for 2027 tokenized stocks is a concession that traditional exchanges cannot build tokenization infrastructure alone, but the 24/5 access promise is a half-measure that preserves clearing bank intermediation rather than enabling true atomic settlement.

deals.summary: Polymarket has reportedly raised $1 billion in a funding round led by 1789 Capital, a firm linked to Donald Trump Jr. This massive capital injection highlights the growing institutional interest in prediction markets and decentralized betting platforms.

Nvidia has entered into a $12.9 billion acquisition deal to acquire Hugging Face. The move is described as both a defensive and offensive strategic maneuver to strengthen its position in the AI ecosystem.

Intercontinental Exchange (ICE), the parent company of the NYSE, is partnering with tZERO to develop infrastructure for a tokenized securities platform. As part of the agreement, ICE will also participate in tZERO's latest funding round.

Hyperliquid Strategies has significantly expanded its equity facility, increasing it from $1 billion to $2.5 billion. This move enhances the firm's capacity to raise capital through the sale of shares.
Kast has launched a business platform powered by stablecoins to facilitate global payments. The platform provides virtual accounts, payment cards, and local payouts across more than 20 currencies.

Strategy has acquired $370 million worth of Bitcoin, marking its first corporate purchase of the asset since June. The company is simultaneously increasing its cash reserves and executing buybacks of its perpetual STRC preferred stock.

Nasdaq-listed DeFi Development Corp is proposing a $20 million preferred stock offering. The company intends to use the raised capital to increase its holdings of Solana and other crypto-related investments.

on_the_radar.title: Harmony to fully sunset Layer 1, proposes token migration to Ethereum for AI video initiative
on_the_radar.summary: Harmony has announced the full sunsetting of its Layer 1 blockchain and is proposing a token migration to Ethereum. The project intends to pivot toward a 'remix economy' focused on AI video creators.

on_the_radar.title: Spot bitcoin ETFs pull in $987 million last week as institutional demand recovers
on_the_radar.summary: Spot Bitcoin ETFs experienced a strong recovery in institutional demand, pulling in $987 million last week. August marked a significant milestone with $3.52 billion in net inflows, the highest monthly total since September 2023.

on_the_radar.title: Pineapple Financial puts $1B in mortgage records on Injective27m
on_the_radar.summary: Pineapple Financial is integrating $1 billion in mortgage records onto the Injective blockchain. This move aims to leverage blockchain technology for the tokenization and management of real-world financial assets.

on_the_radar.title: FinCEN ties $13B in crypto scams to non-US operations
on_the_radar.summary: FinCEN has identified approximately $13 billion in suspected crypto scams based on an analysis of over 33,000 reports filed between 2023 and 2025. The agency specifically linked these fraudulent transactions to operations based outside of the United States.

on_the_radar.title: Solana August 2026 Update
on_the_radar.summary: Solana experienced significant growth in August, with SOL price increasing 41.5% and app revenue jumping to $131.3M. The network successfully conducted its first binding on-chain governance votes, approving a disinflation measure while rejecting a fee burn proposal.

on_the_radar.title: Revolut, OpenReserve get preliminary US bank approval with crypto plans18m, Revolut, OpenReserve get preliminary US bank approval with crypto plansRevolut and OpenReserve received preliminary OCC approval to form US national banks, with both planning cryptocurrency and stablecoin-related services.
on_the_radar.summary: Revolut and OpenReserve have received preliminary approval from the OCC to establish US national banks. Both entities intend to integrate cryptocurrency and stablecoin services into their banking operations.

on_the_radar.title: South Korean regulators introduce tokenized securities roadmap
on_the_radar.summary: South Korean financial regulators have unveiled a three-phase roadmap for the issuance of tokenized assets. This initiative is part of the nation's first comprehensive regulatory framework for tokenized securities, which is expected to become law in 2027.

on_the_radar.title: US bitcoin ETFs report the largest inflow day since January, worth $731 million
on_the_radar.summary: US Bitcoin ETFs experienced their largest single-day inflow since January, totaling $731 million. Analysts link this surge in capital to dovish comments made by Fed Governor Christopher Waller.

on_the_radar.title: US, UK launch joint alliance targeting crypto scam centers9m
on_the_radar.summary: The United States and United Kingdom have established a joint alliance to target and dismantle cryptocurrency scam centers. This international cooperation aims to combat fraudulent schemes and protect investors from digital asset scams.

on_the_radar.title: Coinbase seeks SEC greenlight to list 24/7 equity perpetuals
on_the_radar.summary: Coinbase is seeking approval from the SEC to list 24/7 equity perpetuals. This move aims to bridge traditional equity markets with the continuous trading nature of crypto assets.

on_the_radar.title: Crypto market cap surges to $2.82 trillion as Zcash leads rally alongside stocks
on_the_radar.summary: The total cryptocurrency market capitalization has surged to $2.82 trillion, driven by Bitcoin surpassing the $80,000 mark. Zcash and crypto-related stocks have also seen significant gains amid fluctuating Federal Reserve rate expectations.

on_the_radar.title: Kraken parent Payward partners with SoFi on stablecoin, 24/7 settlement17m
on_the_radar.summary: Payward, the parent company of Kraken, has partnered with SoFi to integrate stablecoin capabilities and enable 24/7 settlement. This collaboration aims to bridge traditional finance with digital assets to improve transaction efficiency.

worth_a_read.title: Solana August 2026 Update
worth_a_read.note: Solana's August update is worth reading to test whether the network's throughput claims are translating into sustained fee revenue, or whether the 'fundamentals' Messari flags for ETH are equally soft on SOL.

worth_a_read.title: ETH August 2026 Update: Flows Recover, Fundamentals Don't
worth_a_read.note: Messari's framing of ETH—flows recovering while fundamentals do not—captures the analytical tension we are seeing across L1s: price action and network usage have decoupled, and the repricing of that gap is the core underwrite for 2026.

worth_a_read.title: 🕙 I Want to Trade Stocks in a Market That Doesn't Sleep: SEC Moves to Update Transfer Agent Rules
worth_a_read.note: Galaxy's analysis of the SEC's transfer agent rule update connects the dots between T+1 settlement pressure and blockchain infrastructure; read it to understand whether this is a genuine on-ramp or a compliance-driven sideshow.

worth_a_read.title: Tokenized Equities on Solana: From Issuance to Execution
worth_a_read.note: This piece on Solana tokenized equities traces the full lifecycle from issuance to execution, and is essential for anyone underwriting whether public chains can capture institutional tokenization volume or will be bypassed by bank-led alternatives.

worth_a_read.title: Revolut clears first hurdle to US banking licence
worth_a_read.note: Revolut's US banking licence progress is a signal on fintech-crypto convergence: if approved, it creates a regulated bridge that current crypto-native banks have struggled to build, and changes the competitive set for stablecoin distribution.

linkedin_post:
The Polymarket raise is not about prediction markets. It is about who gets to run information infrastructure in a second Trump term, and what that costs.

$1 billion, led by 1789 Capital. That is not venture pricing. That is political pricing. The bet is not that Americans will bet more on elections; it is that election-adjacent data flows will be regulated as a utility, not as gambling, and that the firm with the right sponsors gets the concession.

We have seen this movie before in finance. The question is whether crypto founders recognize the genre shift. For two years, the underwriting case for DeFi was technical superiority and regulatory arbitrage. This week, Hyperliquid got a presidential invitation to enter the US market. That is not arbitrage. That is access. The repricing is from "avoids regulation" to "captures regulation."

The parallel story is what banks are building while this political sorting happens. Twenty-one institutions, including BofA and Goldman, targeting a 2027 stablecoin launch. The LSE partnering with Kraken's parent for tokenized stocks, also 2027. South Korea's three-stage securities tokenization plan, stablecoin settlement included. All 2027. Not because the technology requires it, but because that is the political and regulatory horizon they are underwriting.

Our read: the public blockchain layer is being treated as a pilot program. The real capital is flowing to permissioned rails that can absorb the same functionality without the regulatory overhead. The value is shifting from "decentralized" to "decentralized enough for compliance."

What kills this thesis: a single major jurisdiction—say, the EU or Japan—mandating true atomic settlement on public chains for competitive reasons, forcing the bank consortiums to interoperate rather than replace. What confirms it: 2027 arrives and the tokenized stock offerings are custodied on private ledgers with Kraken and others running the API layer.

We are not underwriting technical merit this quarter. We are underwriting regulatory capture speed.
